meta.mechanism: antisense oligonucleotide against apolipoprotein(a) mRNA; inhibits hepatic Lp(a) production
meta.indication: secondary prevention of major adverse cardiovascular events in established CVD (prior MI, ischemic stroke or symptomatic PAD) with Lp(a) >= 70 mg/dL

n_randomized.quote: From December 2019 through July 2022, 14,249 patients were screened and a total of 8,323 patients randomized to either the pelacarsen arm or the placebo arm at 797 sites in 42 countries, across 6 continents.
n_randomized.note: Same number in Novartis release (S1), Ionis 8-K (S2: 'in 8,323 patients with elevated Lp(a) and established CVD') and registry actual enrollment (S4).

median_followup.quote: Randomized patients are followed for clinical endpoints and adverse safety events with a minimum follow-up of 2.5 years and until 993 CEC confirmed primary CV events have accumulated.
median_followup.note: NOT FOUND: median follow-up not disclosed in topline releases. Only design facts available: minimum follow-up 2.5 years; design assumed a follow-up period of approximately 4.25 years; enrollment Dec 2019 to Jul 2022 and registry primary completion 2026-07-16 (S4) imply roughly 4 to 6.6 years of follow-up (derived, not reported).

primary_endpoint.value: time to first CEC-confirmed expanded MACE: CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization requiring hospitalization; tested in overall population (Lp(a) >= 70 mg/dL) and in subpopulation (Lp(a) >= 90 mg/dL)
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary endpoint is a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, and urgent coronary revascularization requiring hospitalization, evaluated in the overall population (Lp(a) ≥70 mg/dL) and subpopulation (Lp(a) ≥90 mg/dL)
primary_endpoint.note: Design paper (S3): 'Successful achievement of the primary objective requires meeting either or both primary objectives.' Key secondary: 3-component MACE.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: established CVD (MI or ischemic stroke >=3 months to <=10 years before screening, or clinically significant symptomatic PAD) and Lp(a) >= 70 mg/dL (approx. 149 nmol/L) at screening by central lab; CV risk factors optimally treated
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Lp(a) ≥ 70 mg/dL at the screening visit, measured at the Central laboratory
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Design paper abstract (S3): 'Established CVD is defined as history of myocardial infarction (MI), ischemic stroke or symptomatic peripheral artery disease.'

planned_events.quote: The study will end when 993 CEC confirmed primary CV events have accumulated.
planned_events.note: Two interim analyses planned at approx. 546 and 745 events (55% and 75%). Whether exactly 993 events accrued at study end is NOT FOUND.

assumed_rrr.quote: The required 993 unique primary endpoint events provide more than 90% power to detect a hazard ratio (HR) of approximately 0.80 for the primary endpoint in the full population or HR of 0.75 in the subpopulation.
assumed_rrr.note: RRR 0.20 derived from HR 0.80 (full population); HR 0.75 (RRR 0.25) in Lp(a) >= 90 mg/dL subpopulation. Placebo annual event rate assumed 4.6%.

power.quote: The required 993 unique primary endpoint events provide more than 90% power

alpha.quote: One-sided testing will be performed and the alpha-adjusted to preserve an overall 1-sided type-I error of 0.025.
alpha.note: One-sided 0.025 (not two-sided). Final analysis one-sided alpha 0.0245 after Bonferroni spending at interims (0.0001 and 0.0004). Dunnett test across co-primary populations.

stopped_early.note: No early stop reported; trial ran to completion. Registry fields, not quotable sentences.

baseline.quote: The median Lp(a) level at baseline was 108.3 mg/dL (235.8 nmol/L).
baseline.note: Table 3 gives median (Q1-Q3) 108.2 (86.60-137.80) mg/dL and 235.7 (203.5-307.7) nmol/L; small text/table discrepancy. Table based on database snapshot of September 09, 2024.

baseline.quote: The median Lp(a) level at baseline was 108.3 mg/dL (235.8 nmol/L).
baseline.note: Paper states the same nmol/L and mg/dL assays are used in Lp(a)HORIZON and cites the conversion nmol/L = 2.18 x mg/dL - 3.83 for approximate thresholds. Table 3 median 235.7 (203.5-307.7) nmol/L.

baseline.quote: The median baseline LDL-C of the patients was 65.7 mg/dL (1.7 mmol/L).
baseline.note: Table 3 gives median (Q1-Q3) LDL-C 64.6 (52.0-80.8) mg/dL; text/table discrepancy. 77.5% on high-intensity statin, 56.6% ezetimibe or bile acid resin, 10.8% PCSK9 inhibitor.

baseline.quote: 78.9% of patients were in the Lp(a) ≥ 90 mg/dL stratum at randomization.

biomarker_effects.method: isoform-independent assay; mean percent change from baseline
biomarker_effects.quote: mean percent decreases of 35% at a dose of 20 mg every 4 weeks, 56% at 40 mg every 4 weeks, 58% at 20 mg every 2 weeks, 72% at 60 mg every 4 weeks, and 80% at 20 mg every week, as compared with 6% with placebo
biomarker_effects.note: 20 mg weekly arm (80 mg total monthly exposure). Not placebo-adjusted; placebo -6%, so approx. -74 percentage points vs placebo (derived). Phase 3 used 80 mg ONCE monthly, not 20 mg weekly; the 80 mg monthly regimen itself was not tested in phase 2.

biomarker_effects.method: isoform-independent assay; mean percent change from baseline
biomarker_effects.note: Highest monthly dose tested in phase 2 (60 mg Q4W). Placebo -6%.

biomarker_effects.method: pharmacodynamic modeling projection (NOT an observed phase 3 value)
biomarker_effects.quote: Pharmacodynamic modeling indicates that this dosage should produce approximately an 80% reduction in time-averaged Lp(a) levels, similar to the 20mg weekly dose studied in phase 2b.
biomarker_effects.note: Expected, not measured. With median baseline 108.3 mg/dL, an 80% reduction corresponds to approx. 87 mg/dL absolute lowering (derived).

biomarker_effects.quote: Lower lipoprotein (a), Lp(a), levels were achieved with pelacarsen in this study population
biomarker_effects.note: NOT FOUND: achieved phase 3 Lp(a) reduction not quantified in Novartis release or Ionis 8-K (S2: 'substantially lower lipoprotein (a) [Lp(a)] levels were achieved with pelacarsen'). Press (S11) reported pelacarsen lowered Lp(a) 'by an average of 72%' in past studies and that analysts said Ionis indicated similar levels in this trial: UNVERIFIED, verified_primary=false. 72% matches the phase 2 60 mg Q4W arm, not the 80 mg/month projection.

hr.quote: did not meet its primary endpoint of reducing the risk of cardiovascular events
hr.note: NOT FOUND: no HR disclosed in topline; full data scheduled for AHA 2026 (Nov 7) per S12.

ci_low.note: NOT FOUND: not disclosed in topline.

ci_high.note: NOT FOUND: not disclosed in topline.

p.note: NOT FOUND: not disclosed in topline.

events_treatment.note: NOT FOUND: not disclosed in topline.

events_control.note: NOT FOUND: not disclosed in topline.

safety_signals.value: acceptable safety profile in phase 3 (no specifics disclosed)
safety_signals.quote: Pelacarsen demonstrated an acceptable safety profile.

safety_signals.value: phase 2: injection-site reactions most common; no differences vs placebo in platelets, liver/renal measures or flu-like symptoms
safety_signals.quote: The most common adverse events were injection-site reactions.

genetics.finding: Two LPA variants (rs10455872, rs3798220) associated with higher Lp(a) and higher coronary disease risk; association abolished after adjusting for Lp(a) level
genetics.quote: We identified a common variant (rs10455872) at the LPA locus with an odds ratio for coronary disease of 1.70 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.49 to 1.95) and another independent variant (rs3798220) with an odds ratio of 1.92 (95% CI, 1.48 to 2.49).

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: CHD benefit proportional to absolute Lp(a) reduction; ~101.5 mg/dL lowering needed to match 1 mmol/L LDL-C lowering
genetics.effect: 10 mg/dL lower genetically predicted Lp(a): OR 0.942 (0.933-0.951); 101.5 mg/dL (71.0-137.0) equivalent to 38.67 mg/dL LDL-C
genetics.quote: Thus, a 101.5-mg/dL change (95% CI, 71.0-137.0) in Lp(a) concentration had the same association with CHD risk as a 38.67-mg/dL change in LDL-C level.

genetics.finding: Lp(a)-GWAS-Consortium MR: required Lp(a) lowering 65.7 mg/dL to match 38.67 mg/dL LDL-C lowering
genetics.quote: We estimated that the required reduction in Lp(a) effect size would be 65.7 mg/dL (95% CI, 46.3-88.3) to reach the same potential effect on clinical outcomes that can be reached by lowering LDL-C by 38.67 mg/dL

consensus_explanation.summary: No consensus exists as of 2026-10-05: only a topline 'primary endpoint not met' statement is public (no HR, CI, event counts or achieved Lp(a) lowering); full results are due at AHA 2026 on 7 Nov. Competing hypotheses: (1) Insufficient absolute Lp(a) lowering (drug_or_dose): MR suggests benefit scales with absolute reduction and ~100 mg/dL (Burgess 2018; 65.7 mg/dL per Lamina 2019) is needed to match a 1 mmol/L LDL-C effect; expected ~80% lowering of a median 108 mg/dL gives ~87 mg/dL, and patients near the 70 mg/dL entry threshold would get far less; ASO lowering (~72-80%) is shallower than siRNAs (>94%); analysts (William Blair) floated 'deeper Lp(a) inhibition' and higher-baseline subgroups. (2) Lp(a) causal theory wrong or not reversible on a ~4-year trial timescale (target): lifelong genetic exposure may not translate to short-term pharmacologic benefit; the result 'raises questions' for the whole class. (3) Design/population: very well-treated background risk (median LDL-C ~65 mg/dL, 77.5% high-intensity statin), a 4-point MACE including stroke (Amgen argues genetics link Lp(a) less strongly to ischemic stroke) and a low-ish 70 mg/dL entry threshold may have diluted any effect. Which applies will depend on the AHA data (achieved absolute lowering, the >=90 mg/dL subpopulation, and dose-response analyses).
consensus_explanation.note_taxonomy: No consensus yet; effect_too_small is the leading hypothesis, not an established answer.

open_questions: Result in the Lp(a) >= 90 mg/dL co-primary subpopulation is not stated explicitly in either release. Novartis (S1) says benefit was not demonstrated 'in the overall study population'; both releases say the trial 'did not meet its primary endpoint'. Because the design (S3) counts success if either co-primary is met, this implies the >=90 mg/dL test also failed, but that is an inference, not a disclosed fact.

Achieved phase 3 Lp(a) lowering is not disclosed. The ~72% figure appears only in press (S11 search snippet, unverified) and equals the phase 2 60 mg Q4W arm. The design paper (S3) projected ~80% time-averaged lowering for 80 mg monthly.
Design paper text vs Table 3 discrepancies: median Lp(a) 108.3 vs 108.2 mg/dL; >=90 mg/dL share 78.9% vs 78.6%; median LDL-C 65.7 vs 64.6 mg/dL (Table 3 based on 9 Sep 2024 snapshot).

AHA 2026 date (7 Nov, 08:30-09:45 CT, primary results plus extended analyses) comes from a news listing (S12), not from Novartis or AHA directly; Novartis/Ionis say only 'an upcoming medical congress'.
Phase 3 regimen (80 mg once monthly) was never directly tested in phase 2; phase 2 tested 20 mg weekly (-80%) and 60 mg Q4W (-72%). The 80% expectation rests on PD modeling (S3).
Whether 993 adjudicated events were reached at close-out, and the median follow-up, are not disclosed.

Burgess 2018 pub_date uses Europe PMC first-publication date (journal issue 2018-07-01); online-first date may be earlier (not verified). Clarke 2009 pub_date is the NEJM issue date (24 Dec 2009); Europe PMC lists 2009-12-01.
Hypothesis that background GLP-1/SGLT2/PCSK9 use diluted benefit appears only in secondary news (allsci.com, 2026-09-08) and was not attributed to a verifiable primary statement; not used.
